front.title: Depth and Fanout Bounding for Agent-to-Agent Discovery Forwarding

abstract.t: This document describes a mechanism, deployed in production as part of the "AI Docking Port" discovery protocol, for bounding the traffic cost of stateless agent-to-agent forwarding across a network of independent nodes with no central registry. When a node forwards a request to its neighbors, and those neighbors may forward again, request cost grows as fanout^depth; absent an explicit bound this cost is paid by relaying operators rather than the requester. This document specifies two operator-controlled limits, max_depth and max_fanout, published in a node's discovery manifest, and the forwarding behavior they constrain. It is submitted for discussion as a possible contribution to ongoing community work on agent discovery and invocation protocols, including the W3C Community Group "AI Agent Protocol".
